questions.q: What does an RNN's hidden state represent?
options: The final prediction of the network
A vector that summarizes the tokens read so far
The list of all training examples
The learning rate at the current step
questions.explain: The hidden state is updated at every token and carries a running summary of the sequence forward.

questions.q: In the lesson's experiment, only the first token of a sequence was changed. What happened to its effect on the final hidden state as the sequence got longer?
options: It grew larger
It stayed the same
It shrank toward zero
It flipped sign at every step
questions.explain: The effect fell from about 1e-1 at length 2 to about 4e-12 at length 40: early information vanishes in a plain RNN.

questions.q: What are the steps of attention for one position?
options: Score against every position, softmax into weights, weighted average of values
Sort the tokens alphabetically, then take the first one
Multiply the hidden state by itself repeatedly
Pick the single most recent token and ignore the rest
questions.explain: Attention scores the query against all keys, normalizes with a softmax, and averages the value vectors with those weights.

questions.q: Why can attention learn long-range links that a plain RNN struggles with?
options: It uses a larger learning rate
It removes the need for any weights
It only ever looks at the previous token
Every token has a direct one-step path to every other token
questions.explain: In an RNN the path from an early token to a late one is as long as the sequence; attention connects any two positions directly.

questions.q: What is the main cost of comparing every token with every other token?
options: Compute grows with the square of the sequence length
The model can no longer be trained on a GPU
The weights must be stored as text
Word order is lost completely
questions.explain: All-pairs comparison scales quadratically with length, which is one reason context windows are limited.
